candidate_relations.reason: The clinical course (6-month progression post-mild COVID-19, cavitation with halo, pleural/subpleural abscess, bronchopleural fistula, pneumothorax) and the invasive histopathology (degenerated hyphae in pleural/subpleural abscess) are more consistent with SAIA than classic CPA. While CPA shares cavitation features, SAIA is the recognized subtype for this semi-invasive presentation in a mildly immunocompromised host. The pneumothorax complication is also omitted.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Chronic Pulmonary Aspergillosis (CPA) is a related but distinct subtype from Subacute Invasive Aspergillosis (SAIA); SAIA is a semi-invasive form with progression over 1–3 months in mildly immunocompromised hosts, whereas CPA typically progresses over >3 months in non-immunocompromised hosts with structural lung disease; additionally, the pneumothorax component is absent

candidate_relations.label: Aspergilloma
candidate_relations.reason: The admission CT does note interval progression of an aspergilloma, but the overall diagnosis is SAIA with invasive pleural extension and pneumothorax. Aspergilloma alone is a manifestation/component finding and does not represent the full diagnostic entity requested.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Aspergilloma describes a fungal ball within a pre-existing cavity and is a component/finding noted on the admission CT, but it does not capture the invasive disease process (SAIA), the pleural/subpleural abscess, or the pneumothorax

case_quality_flags: SAIA and CPA distinction can be nuanced; the 6-month subacute timeline and mild immunosuppression (post-COVID) with invasive histopathology favor SAIA over CPA
Negative galactomannan and negative fungal cultures from surgical specimens are atypical for invasive aspergillosis but consistent with SAIA where tissue invasion may be limited
